title: E2E: Efficient Filtered AKNN Search via Adaptive Termination

problem.claim: Filtered AKNN search retrieves nearest vectors under attribute constraints.

gap.claim: Fixed termination conditions search the entire index, causing redundant computation and missing early-termination opportunities for easy queries.

contributions.claim: A lightweight model estimates filtered-AKNN search cost to enable adaptive termination.
Early-probing information, including attribute distributions and intermediate distance statistics, is used to predict overall search cost.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on six real-world datasets report 1.1–3.7× speedup over state-of-the-art baselines at 95% recall while maintaining search accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: AKNN search is widely used in vector databases, including filtered search under attribute constraints.
Existing fixed termination searches the entire index and performs redundant computation because query difficulty varies.
A lightweight cost model adaptively terminates easy queries earlier and searches harder queries longer.
The model predicts search cost from information gathered during early probing.
Experiments on six real-world datasets report speedups at 95% recall while maintaining search accuracy.

source_observation.claim: Search effort varies across filtered AKNN queries, and early-probing statistics can predict overall search cost.

interpretation.claim: Adaptive termination can reduce computation when query difficulty is estimated reliably.

application.claim: Systems with variable query difficulty may benefit from lightweight early-stage cost estimation tied to termination decisions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how prediction errors affect accuracy or when adaptive termination fails.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the cost-model architecture or training procedure.
The six datasets, baselines, and experimental protocol are not identified.
The meaning of maintaining search accuracy and the trade-off between latency and recall are not detailed.
